data.name: House of Evil
data.detailed_description:
House of Evil - atmospheric survival horror with a first-person view, in which you can test your nerves for strength. The events take place in the mansion that exists in reality. The main character is an ordinary philistine, his wife is an exorcist, after an unusual telephone conversation, the protagonist can not call to the spouse, and decides to go in search of her, fate takes him to an old mansion where unimaginable things begin to happen. Four horsemen of the apocalypse moved into the owners of this mansion, if the riders get out on freedom - come the end of the world. The last hope of humanity is our main hero. You will have to solve interesting puzzles, mix herbs, create different potions, consecrate water, study spells in Latin, and use it all against evil spirits, demons and other evil spirits.

You will find more than 40 rooms of the mansion where the events unfold games. Two floors of the mansion, a terrible cellar where a psychiatrist conducted his rituals, over mentally ill people, from his hospital. According to the plot, a psychiatrist is the brother of the owner of the mansion. Cemetery on the territory of the mansion, another for the mirror world, in which we get in the middle of the game. Another world, it is a copy of the real world, only everything that is gloomy and evil in it.

Manor Zaklyuchye is located in the Tver region,Russia, if you go on M-10 from Moscow to St. Petersburg, and before the city of Valdai and the Valdai lake turn to Borovichi, and before reaching it 50 km there will be a station Likoshino. Here, in a secret corner, on the shore of the forest lake is this mansion. In the late XIX - early XX century here, in the village of Zaklyuchye, was built a manor of the St. Petersburg architect A.S. Khrenova, probably, on his own project. The main house has a complex asymmetric configuration of the plan and consists of various volumes. Due to its remoteness, beautiful tiled stoves and a spiral staircase of iron are preserved inside the house. And on the territory there were amusing sculptures of the Soviet period, when there was still a tuberculosis sanatorium, during the Soviet period, not one patient perished in this mansion. However, this mansion also became famous for the mysterious disappearance of people. And with its eerie atmosphere from which the blood runs cold. The circle of the mansion encompasses a dense forest. It remains to guess what happened to the disappeared people, whether they got lost in the forest, although no traces were found by search units , whether it is related to the individual reduction.

There is a system of using "first-aid kits" and potions for "banishment" that has a certain complexity. The player can find five types of herbs: wormwood, Yarrow, St. John's wort, Basil, Blagovonia. With a certain mixing of herbs, a potion that restores health, or a potion that weakens the immunity of enemies . Also, in the game will have to consecrate water and much more.

reviews.review:
House of Evil is a first-person survival horror adventure that combines supernatural mysteries, occult rituals, and psychological tension within an abandoned mansion. Developed and published by VikTor, the game follows a desperate search for a missing woman that gradually develops into a confrontation with terrifying forces threatening humanity. Its ambitious premise incorporates religious symbolism, paranormal entities, and historical inspiration into an experience focused on exploration, puzzle-solving, and survival. While its creative ideas are intriguing, the execution struggles to deliver the polished and consistently frightening experience that its concept promises.

The story follows a man whose wife, an exorcist, mysteriously disappears following a troubling telephone conversation. Determined to uncover the truth, he travels to an isolated mansion where disturbing supernatural events have taken place. His investigation eventually reveals connections to the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse, transforming a personal rescue mission into a struggle against potentially catastrophic forces. This narrative foundation provides an interesting combination of family tragedy, forbidden rituals, and supernatural mythology. Unfortunately, the characters receive limited development, making the emotional stakes less compelling than they could have been. The mystery surrounding the mansion remains interesting, but the storytelling lacks the depth necessary to make its revelations truly memorable.

One distinctive aspect is the game's inspiration from Manor Zaklyuchye, a historical estate in Russia's Tver region. This real-world influence gives the fictional setting additional personality and mystery. The narrative incorporates disturbing accounts of psychiatric experiments, unexplained disappearances, and occult practices, creating an unsettling connection between human cruelty and supernatural corruption. These ideas provide excellent opportunities for environmental storytelling, particularly when exploring rooms associated with the mansion's former occupants. However, the historical background is not explored extensively enough to fully capitalize on its fascinating premise.

Exploration represents a substantial portion of the gameplay, with players investigating more than forty rooms spread across two floors. Additional environments include a sinister basement, a cemetery, and locations connected to an alternate reality. The interconnected mansion encourages careful observation, item collection, and investigation, while the surrounding areas introduce additional mysteries. The mirror world is particularly interesting because it presents a distorted version of familiar surroundings, reinforcing the impression that reality itself has become corrupted. Nevertheless, navigation can occasionally become frustrating when objectives are unclear or important items are difficult to locate. These moments interrupt the atmosphere and make progression feel unnecessarily tedious.

The gameplay distinguishes itself through an emphasis on supernatural knowledge rather than conventional combat. Players must investigate paranormal phenomena, study Latin incantations, bless water, and prepare special substances to confront hostile entities. These mechanics complement the exorcism-centered storyline and provide an unusual alternative to traditional survival horror encounters. Preparing for supernatural threats through rituals and resource management is conceptually appealing, but the execution sometimes lacks clarity. Certain interactions feel awkward, while insufficient guidance can turn potentially satisfying discoveries into repetitive experimentation.

The herbal crafting system introduces another layer of survival mechanics. Players collect ingredients such as wormwood, yarrow, St. John's wort, and basil to create mixtures with different effects. Some preparations restore health, while others weaken supernatural enemies. This encourages exploration and provides a practical purpose for gathering resources. However, the crafting process could benefit from clearer explanations, more intuitive controls, and stronger feedback. Although the system adds variety, it does not always feel sufficiently refined to become a consistently enjoyable part of the experience.

Atmosphere is one of the game's more appealing qualities. Its isolated location, gloomy interiors, disturbing imagery, and occult mythology create an environment suitable for supernatural horror. The first-person perspective strengthens the feeling of vulnerability, particularly when investigating dark corridors and unfamiliar rooms. The basement and alternate dimension offer particularly effective foundations for psychological discomfort. Unfortunately, suspense is not always maintained consistently. Repetitive exploration, uneven pacing, and limited presentation quality occasionally weaken the tension. The game demonstrates an understanding of traditional haunted-house horror, but its frightening moments lack the consistency necessary to sustain genuine dread throughout the adventure.

Visually, House of Evil reflects the limitations of a modest independent production. Some environments successfully communicate abandonment and supernatural decay, while others lack convincing detail and refinement. Animation quality, environmental interactions, and overall technical presentation can feel dated compared with more polished horror experiences. These shortcomings become particularly noticeable because exploration and object interaction are central to progression. Although the game does not require cutting-edge graphics to establish an unsettling atmosphere, smoother mechanics and stronger visual consistency would have considerably improved immersion.

Steam Deck compatibility remains unverified, with no confirmed official compatibility classification established here. The game was primarily designed for Windows, and running it on Steam Deck may require Proton compatibility support. Controller functionality, interface readability, and performance should therefore be considered uncertain rather than guaranteed. Players interested in experiencing the game on Valve's handheld should anticipate possible configuration adjustments.

Overall, House of Evil is an ambitious but uneven horror adventure with several creative ideas that deserve recognition. Its historically inspired mansion, supernatural storyline, occult rituals, and herbal crafting provide an interesting foundation, but limited characterization, confusing progression, and inconsistent technical polish prevent it from reaching its full potential. Enthusiasts of obscure independent horror games may appreciate its unusual concepts and unsettling environments, while players seeking refined mechanics and consistently effective scares may find it disappointing. Despite its shortcomings, the game offers a distinctive interpretation of supernatural survival horror.

Its atmosphere and imaginative premise are appealing, but the execution lacks the refinement necessary to make it a genuinely memorable horror experience.

Rating: 4/10
